subject: Transition plan: live-sync for streaming + tool-calls (schema alignment)
messages:
From: Alexander Nguyen <alexander.nguyen@glyph.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@glyph.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Glyph x Redwood — kickoff & ramp request for live-sync streaming

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the streaming & tool-calling demo sold our eng team on Redwood's latency guarantees. We'd like to start a short ramp to move a limited subset of Glyph's inference traffic to Redwood's hosted runtime. Our immediate asks:

- Streaming ingestion for short-form clinical notes (avg 220 tokens) with partial results delivered every 250ms.
- Function/tool-calls for a medical-coding microservice (sync + idempotency & retry semantics).
- Structured outputs: a JSON schema for the extracted entities and confidence scores (we included samples).

I've attached an initial integration_spec_v1.json and a spreadsheet with proposed milestones (proposed_milestones.xlsx). Priya (cc) will be our technical PM for the project.

High-level target: pilot route traffic in 2–3 weeks, then a 4-week validation window. Can we get a mutual action plan and a short checklist for schema validation, streaming chunking, and tool-call retries? Also, any constraints we should watch for on the Redwood side (max tokens per chunk, KV cache TTL, etc.)?

Thanks,
Alex
Alexander Nguyen
Head of Platform Integrations, Glyph AI
Attachments: integration_spec_v1.json (application/json), proposed_milestones.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alexander Nguyen <alexander.nguyen@glyph.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@glyph.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Glyph x Redwood — kickoff & ramp request for live-sync streaming

Alex / Priya — great to get this started. Looping in Camila (CS lead) and Marissa (implementation PM) so we can align on the MLP (minimum lovable product) for the pilot.

Quick answers up-front:
- Streaming: Redwood supports partial-token streaming with a recommended max chunk interval of ~200–300ms for sub-500-token responses; that maps well to your 250ms target. We generally recommend a 1–2KB chunk size cap to avoid reassembly work on the client.
- Tool-calls: we treat tool-calls as best-effort idempotent operations when you provide a call_id. Recommended retry: exponential backoff with 3 attempts. We can wire an at-most-once wrapper if the tool is non-idempotent, but that needs coordination.
- JSON schema validation: we can run schema checks at both sandbox and validation stages; please provide the canonical schema and a small corpus of example payloads (ndjson preferred).

Next proposed steps (we'll draft a short MAP):
1) Camila will produce a 6-point mutual action plan (milestones, owners, success criteria).
2) Marissa will prepare an implementation checklist (sandbox keys, example requests, webhook endpoints).
3) Glyph to provide sample events + schema (you've attached integration_spec_v1.json — we'll ingest).
4) Redwood will provision a pilot route and share a short test harness (TLS cert + streaming client examples).

Can we do a 30-min technical sync on Monday 22 Jul? Proposed window: 10–11am PT.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | soojin_lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Glyph x Redwood — kickoff & ramp request for live-sync streaming

Team — thanks, all. Per the sync just now, I've sketched a mutual action plan (short version) and an itemized checklist for schema alignment. Copy of the MAP:

MAP (short)
- Week 0 (sandbox): sandbox route, sample harness, schema ingestion (owner: Marissa)
- Week 1 (pilot traffic 1%): streaming validation, tool-call contract test, latency baseline (owner: Camila)
- Week 2 (ramp to 10%): monitoring + cost checks, fallback plan validation (owner: Camila)
- Week 3–4 (validation window): quality checks vs. baseline, automated regression tests (owner: Glyph + Redwood)

Schema alignment checklist (items):
- Canonical JSON schema (draft v0.2) — Redwood to run ajv validation during sandbox runs.
- Event envelope: {request_id, timestamp_iso, user_context, input_text, meta} — we need sample ndjson lines for each event type.
- Structured output contract: array of entities with fields {type, span_start, span_end, value, confidence}. Provide edge cases (overlapping spans, nested entities).
- Tool-call contract: call_id, tool_name, payload, retry_hint. We require an idempotency key (call_id) unless the tool supports explicit dedupe on your side.

Marissa — please drop the sandbox keys and the test harness link to the Drive workspace. Alex / Priya — can you add a small set (~50) of representative ndjson lines and flag 3 tricky cases (e.g., nested entity spans, simultaneous tools)? That'll speed validation.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: sample_mvp_schema.json (created during call)

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@glyph.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Glyph x Redwood — kickoff & ramp request for live-sync streaming

Thanks Camila — attaching the sample_event_payloads.ndjson (50 lines) in the Drive link and a short note on the two tricky cases we found. Quick question on retries for tool-calls: if Redwood recommends 3 attempts with exponential backoff, what does Redwood suggest for the TTL on a call_id-based dedupe window? Our tool is plausible at 15s cold processing, but upstream retries could overlap. Are you recommending a sliding window keyed by call_id, or should we include a timestamp and let Redwood dedupe for a fixed 30s window?

We also noticed in the integration_spec a note about KV cache TTL — what default do you set and can we tune it per-route?

— Priya
Priya Sharma
Staff Technical PM, Glyph AI
Attachments: sample_event_payloads.ndjson (ndjson)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@glyph.ai>, Alexander Nguyen <alexander.nguyen@glyph.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Glyph x Redwood — kickoff & ramp request for live-sync streaming

Priya — good questions, thanks for flagging. TL;DR: we recommend a 45s dedupe window keyed by call_id for your workload, and a per-route KV cache TTL default of 60s (tunable). Details: 

- Tool-call dedupe: use call_id + server-side sliding window of 45s. That accommodates 15s cold processing plus a couple of retries and clock drift. If you can provide monotonic processing ids or a dedupe-on-producer signal, we can reduce the window to 20–30s.
- Retries: exponential backoff at 300ms -> 900ms -> 2700ms (three attempts) preserves low tail while avoiding thundering retries. If you need stronger guarantees we can enable an at-most-once wrapper that persists call results for 60s.
- KV cache TTL: default 60s per route (useful for prefix caching and short-term KV items). You can set per-route TTLs in the pilot config if some event types are more cache-friendly.

Action items:
- Marissa: post sandbox keys and pilot-route name to Drive by EOD.
- Camila: I'll review the ndjson edge cases and post comments in the Drive doc.
- Alex / Priya: confirm the 45s dedupe window and whether you'd like the at-most-once wrapper for the medical-coding tool.

I'll also add a short RB (runbook) note in the workspace describing the recommended retry/backoff settings.

— Soojin
